patients.summary: Elementary school teacher with class I obesity who joined the practice in 2016. Three pregnancies under an outside OB group: a 2019-2020 pregnancy with a short cervix ending in a term vaginal birth, a 2022 pregnancy lost at 23 weeks to fetal osteogenesis imperfecta (COL1A1), and a 2025-2026 pregnancy with diet-controlled gestational diabetes ending in cesarean for arrest of labor; postpartum glucose tolerance normal.

documents.title: New Patient Visit - Establish Care
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Robin is 25, new to us, here to establish care and get a physical. Teaches second grade in town. Previously followed by a family doctor near her hometown, last physical about a year ago; she thinks the Pap there in 2015 was normal. Records release signed today.

No active complaints. Feels well. Says her weight has crept up since college, maybe 15-20 lb over a few years. Walks most weekends, no structured exercise during the school year. Eats lunch at school, lots of snacking in the afternoon by her account.

PMH: none other than weight. No surgeries. No hospitalizations.
Meds: none. No supplements.
Allergies: NKDA.
FH: maternal grandmother with type 2 diabetes. Parents well as far as she knows. No known bone or genetic disorders in the family.
SH: married, lives in Amherst. Never smoked. Doesn't drink. No drugs.
Gyn: regular cycles. Not currently trying to conceive, would like to in the next few years.
Vaccines: childhood series and HPV done as a teen per her mother; Tdap about 2 years ago - will confirm from records.

ROS negative in full.

Exam: vitals as charted, BMI 31. Well appearing. HEENT normal, sclerae white, TMs clear. Neck supple, no thyroid enlargement. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender, no masses. Extremities without edema. Skin without acanthosis. Mood and affect normal.

A/P
1. Preventive: CBC, CMP, lipids, TSH, A1c. HIV and hep C screen once - she agrees. Flu shot today. Pap not due until next year per her report; will confirm with records.
2. Obesity, class I (BMI 31). Talked through realistic goals - cut the afternoon snacking, aim for 150 min/wk walking. She'd like to try on her own. Recheck next year.
3. Preconception: when she is ready to try, start a prenatal vitamin a few months ahead. Let us know.

RTC 1 yr or sooner.

documents.body: Hi Robin, nice to meet you this week. All of your blood work came back normal - blood counts, kidney and liver tests, thyroid, cholesterol and the diabetes screen (A1c). HIV and hepatitis C screens were negative. Nothing to do except keep working on the walking. See you next fall.

OUTSIDE OB/GYN GROUP - PRENATAL VISIT
Date of service: 11/01/2019
Patient: Robin Parsons, DOB 02/17/1991
G1P0 at 22w0d by LMP (5/31/19), consistent with 8-week ultrasound. EDD 03/06/2020.

Interval: Pregnancy has gone smoothly to date. Denies vaginal bleeding, loss of fluid, or contractions. Good fetal movement.

Medications: prenatal vitamin with iron, 1 tab PO daily.
Allergies: NKDA.
PMH: obesity, pre-pregnancy BMI 32. PSH: none.
Family history: maternal grandmother with type 2 DM. No family history of osteogenesis imperfecta or skeletal dysplasia.
Social: elementary school teacher. Never smoker, no alcohol.
Immunizations up to date; influenza given 10/2019 at PCP.

Vitals: BP 120/78, HR 72.
FHT normal, in the 140s by Doppler.
Prenatal labs (initial OB panel) reviewed and unremarkable.

Transvaginal ultrasound for cervical length: cervical length 20 mm. No funneling. Placenta posterior, no previa, no placental abnormality.

Assessment: IUP at 22w0d. Short cervix (20 mm) on TVUS.
Plan: Reviewed what a short cervix means and preterm labor warning signs - regular cramping, pelvic pressure, fluid or bleeding should prompt an L&D call. Continue prenatal vitamin. Routine follow-up per schedule; glucose screening at 24-28 weeks.

documents.title: Question about my OB visit
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi, I know you got the note from my OB. They told me my cervix is short and I keep googling and scaring myself. Should I be on bed rest? I'm on my feet all day with 7-year-olds. Sorry to bother you with an OB thing.

documents.title: RE: Question about my OB visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Not a bother at all. I did see the note. Bed rest isn't something we recommend anymore for a short cervix - it hasn't been shown to help and it has its own risks. The main thing is knowing the warning signs your OB went over (regular cramping, pressure, fluid or bleeding) and calling L&D right away if they happen. Your OB is the right person for the day-to-day plan, including anything about work, so please bring the teaching question to your next visit there. I'm glad to talk anytime too.

documents.title: Obstetrics prenatal visit, 22 weeks (visit date 10/20/2022)
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
OUTSIDE OB/GYN GROUP - PRENATAL VISIT
Date of service: 10/20/2022
Patient: Robin Parsons, DOB 02/17/1991
G2P1001 at 22w0d by LMP (5/19/22), dated by first-trimester ultrasound.

Reason: Routine 22-week visit and follow-up of the abnormal 18-week anatomy ultrasound.

History: Her first pregnancy was complicated by a short cervix at 22 weeks but went to term with a vaginal delivery of a healthy daughter (2020). This pregnancy was uneventful until the 18-week anatomy survey (9/22/2022), which showed fractures of multiple long bones including both femurs and both humeri, a hypoplastic thorax, limb deformities and fetal growth restriction. She reports no trauma and no infections or febrile illness this pregnancy. She is understandably worried and asks what this means for the baby and why it happened.

Medications: prenatal vitamin with iron, 1 tab daily.
Allergies: NKDA.
PMH: obesity (pre-pregnancy BMI 32). Short cervix in prior pregnancy. PSH: none.
Family history: no known genetic disorders or bone disease in either family.
Social: teacher; never smoker; no alcohol.

Vitals stable, within normal limits.
Fundal height appropriate for gestational age. FHT normal by Doppler.

Labs today (maternal): calcium 9.2 mg/dL (8.6-10.2), phosphate 3.5 mg/dL (2.5-4.5), alkaline phosphatase 90 IU/L (30-120 in pregnancy). Maternal bone chemistry normal.

Assessment: IUP at 22w0d with fetal skeletal findings (multiple long-bone fractures, small thorax, limb deformity, FGR) most suggestive of a fetal skeletal dysplasia, likely osteogenesis imperfecta.
Plan: Urgent maternal-fetal medicine consultation with detailed ultrasound and genetics counseling - scheduled 10/25. Discussed in general terms that the findings can carry a serious prognosis and that MFM and genetics will go over this in detail, including testing options. Support resources provided.

cc: Primary care physician

documents.title: Outside OB note reviewed
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: OB 22-wk note: fetal long-bone fractures, small chest, FGR - suspected fetal OI. Maternal Ca/phos/alk phos normal. MFM consult 10/25. Problem list updated. Will call her after MFM.

documents.title: Maternal-fetal medicine consultation (visit date 10/25/2022)
documents.author: maternal-fetal medicine
documents.body:
MATERNAL-FETAL MEDICINE CONSULTATION
Regional hospital MFM service
Date of service: 10/25/2022
Referring: outside OB/GYN group. cc: PCP

Dear colleagues,
We saw Ms. Parsons, a 31-year-old G2P1001 at 22w5d, for evaluation of fetal skeletal abnormalities identified at her 18-week anatomy survey.

Detailed ultrasound today: Single live intrauterine pregnancy. Biometry lags dates, consistent with growth restriction. Long bones are short and angulated, with evidence of multiple fractures involving both femurs and both humeri. The thorax is small with a reduced thoracic-to-abdominal circumference ratio, consistent with a hypoplastic thoracic cavity. Limb deformities are present. Cardiac activity present.

Impression: The constellation is most consistent with perinatal lethal osteogenesis imperfecta (type II). Pulmonary hypoplasia from the small chest is the main determinant of prognosis.

Counseling: We met with Ms. Parsons and her husband for an extended visit together with genetic counseling. We reviewed the likely diagnosis, that the expected outcome is not compatible with long-term survival, and the options of continuing the pregnancy with comfort-focused perinatal care or ending the pregnancy by induction of labor. We reviewed that most cases arise from a new (de novo) dominant change in a collagen gene. After discussion she elected amniocentesis for diagnostic confirmation, performed today under ultrasound guidance without complication. Results are expected in about two weeks.

She will let us know her decision regarding the pregnancy; we will coordinate with her OB team and labor and delivery.

Thank you for involving us in her care.
Maternal-Fetal Medicine

documents.title: Genetics results letter (dated 11/14/2022)
documents.author: genetics
documents.body:
MEDICAL GENETICS - RESULTS LETTER
Date: 11/14/2022
Re: Robin Parsons, DOB 02/17/1991 (pregnancy sample)

Dear Ms. Parsons and colleagues,
This letter summarizes our phone discussion of the amniocentesis results from 10/25/2022.

Result: Sequencing of the collagen genes COL1A1 and COL1A2 identified a heterozygous pathogenic variant in COL1A1 (a glycine substitution within the triple-helical domain). This result confirms osteogenesis imperfecta and, together with the ultrasound findings, is consistent with the perinatal lethal form (type II).

Interpretation and recurrence: Ms. Parsons has no features of osteogenesis imperfecta herself - no history of fractures, white sclerae and normal hearing by her report - and there is no family history of bone disease. The variant is therefore presumed to have arisen de novo in this pregnancy. Because a small proportion of apparently de novo cases are explained by germline mosaicism in a parent, the recurrence risk in a future pregnancy is low, under 5 percent, but higher than the general population risk.

Recommendations for a future pregnancy: early referral to maternal-fetal medicine, with an early and a detailed anatomy ultrasound focused on the fetal skeleton; diagnostic testing for this familial variant is available if desired.

Please contact us with any questions.
Medical Genetics
cc: OB/GYN; PCP

documents.title: Genetics letter reviewed
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: COL1A1 pathogenic variant, OI type II confirmed in the pregnancy. Presumed de novo; recurrence <5% (possible germline mosaicism). Future pregnancy: early MFM referral. Noted in problem list comment - remember when she next calls with a pregnancy.

Robin is here 3 weeks after delivering at 23w6d (induction 11/1, stillborn 11/2) for a pregnancy affected by OI type II - COL1A1 variant confirmed on amnio, presumed de novo per genetics.

Physically: bleeding has stopped, no fever, breast engorgement resolved. Saw her OB last week - told recovery is on track.

Emotionally: sad, cries most days, but says she is "functioning" - caring for her daughter, eating, sleeping 6 hours or so. Not anhedonic about everything; enjoys time with her daughter. Going back to her classroom after Thanksgiving and is nervous about questions from colleagues. She and her husband have been to one session with the hospital's bereavement group and plan to keep going. No SI, no thoughts of self-harm. No alcohol.

PHQ-9 5 (sleep, mood, energy).
Meds: prenatal vitamin with iron - she asked if she should keep taking it; I said that's fine either way, reasonable to continue if they might try again.
Bivalent COVID booster at pharmacy 10/15 - recorded.

Exam: Vitals as charted. Tearful at times, appropriate, good eye contact. Heart regular, lungs clear. Abd soft, nontender.

A/P
1. Grief after second-trimester loss - this is a normal grief response; no depression diagnosis. Continue bereavement group. Reviewed when to reach out sooner (not sleeping, can't get through work, hopeless, any thoughts of self-harm). Offered counseling referral; she'll think about it and message.
2. Hx of pregnancy affected by fetal OI - genetics recommends early MFM in any future pregnancy. Noted.
3. Return-to-work note if the school asks.
4. Follow up in 6-8 weeks or sooner; physical next fall.

documents.body: To whom it may concern: Robin Parsons was under my care for a medical leave in November 2022. She was cleared to return to full duty without restrictions as of 11/28/2022. Please contact the office with any questions.

documents.title: RE: Note for school
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: No hassle at all - letter is attached and in your documents. Glad to hear things are a little better. We never got that follow-up booked; I'll have the front desk offer you a time, and you can always just message.

reports.text: Specimen: cervical, liquid-based preparation. Specimen adequacy: satisfactory for evaluation; transformation zone component present. Interpretation: negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy. High-risk HPV (cobas, including types 16 and 18): not detected.

documents.title: Annual Physical with Pap/HPV
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Annual exam.

32 y/o, here for physical. Last seen 11/2022 after her loss; the planned follow-up never got scheduled. She says the spring was hard but things feel steadier now - kept going to the bereavement group through June, back to herself at school. Daughter started preschool. They have not decided about another pregnancy; if they do, she knows to message early so we can get her to MFM. Still taking prenatal vitamin most days.

No new symptoms. Weight about the same as last year. Swimming at the town pool this summer, 2-3x/wk.

Meds: prenatal vitamin with iron daily. NKDA.
SH: married, teacher, never smoker, no EtOH.
PHQ-2 0.
Pap overdue (last 2018).

Exam: BMI 33. Well appearing, bright affect. HEENT nl. Neck no LAD or thyromegaly. CV RRR no murmur. Lungs clear. Abd soft NT. Pelvic: normal external genitalia and vagina, parous cervix without lesions, Pap/HPV collected; bimanual normal. Ext no edema.

A/P
1. Health maintenance: Pap with HPV co-test today. CBC, lipids, A1c. Flu shot today; updated COVID vaccine when available at the pharmacy.
2. Obesity class I (BMI 33): stable. She likes swimming; encouraged keeping something going through winter. Revisit in 6 months - she agreed to a spring check.
3. Hx pregnancy affected by fetal OI (COL1A1, presumed de novo): early MFM referral with any pregnancy.
4. Mood: much improved, screen negative today.
RTC 6 months (weight), 1 yr physical.

documents.title: Results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Robin - Pap normal and HPV negative, so the next one is in 5 years. Blood counts and cholesterol fine, A1c normal. Front desk will set up the spring check-in.

documents.title: COVID shot
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Got the new COVID shot on 10/14 at the pharmacy (Pfizer). Just letting you know for my records.

documents.title: RE: COVID shot
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Thanks, added to your immunization record.

documents.title: Missed appointment
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Hi Robin, we missed you yesterday at 3:45. Would you like to reschedule your check-in?

documents.title: RE: Missed appointment
documents.author: patient
documents.body: So sorry!! Parent conferences ran late and I completely forgot. Honestly nothing new to report - can we just do it at my physical in September?

documents.title: RE: Missed appointment
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: No problem, you're booked for your physical 9/17 at 3:40.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Annual. 33F.

Interval: well, no illnesses. Skipped the spring check (conferences). Weight unchanged from last year. Kept swimming until October last year then stopped; walks at lunch with another teacher now.

They are thinking about trying again next year. Reviewed plan: message as soon as she has a positive test, we confirm and send her to OB and MFM together for early and detailed scans per genetics. Continue prenatal vitamin with iron.

Meds: prenatal vitamin with iron daily. NKDA.
PHQ-2 0. Mood good.
Never smoker, no alcohol.

Exam: BMI 33. Well. HEENT normal. Thyroid not enlarged. CV regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft. No edema. Skin no acanthosis.

A/P
1. Obesity class I (BMI 33) - pre-pregnancy counseling: even modest loss before conception lowers GDM risk; she has her grandmother's diabetes in mind. Offered nutrition referral again - declined, wants to try a meal-planning approach with her husband.
2. Labs: CMP, lipids, A1c.
3. Flu shot today. Updated COVID at pharmacy.
4. Pap/HPV next 2028.
RTC 1 yr or with a positive pregnancy test.

documents.title: Lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Robin, labs look fine. A1c normal (under 5.7). Kidney, liver and cholesterol normal.

documents.title: Covid vaccine
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Updated covid shot Saturday 10/19, pharmacy. For your records!

documents.title: Positive test
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi - positive test this morning. LMP April 20. You told me to message right away so here I am. Excited and nervous. Still on the prenatal.

documents.title: RE: Positive test
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Congratulations, Robin - and thank you for letting me know early. Let's see you next week to confirm, and I'll send the OB and maternal-fetal medicine referrals the same day so the early scans get scheduled. Keep taking the prenatal.

documents.title: Office Visit - Pregnancy Confirmation
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
34 y/o G3P1101 with positive home test 5/22. LMP 4/20/25 -> 5w4d, EDD ~1/25/26. Planned. Mild fatigue and nausea, no vomiting. No bleeding or cramping.

OB history:
- G1 2019-20: short cervix (20 mm) at 22 wks, term SVD 2/2020, healthy daughter.
- G2 2022: fetal OI type II (COL1A1 pathogenic variant on amnio, presumed de novo); induction, stillbirth at 23w6d, 11/2022. Genetics: recurrence <5% (germline mosaicism), early MFM and detailed skeletal imaging in future pregnancies.

Meds: prenatal vitamin with iron daily. NKDA. No tobacco or alcohol.
Pre-pregnancy weight today, BMI 32. FH: maternal grandmother T2DM.

Exam: vitals as charted. Well, a bit anxious. Abd soft, nontender.
Urine hCG positive.

A/P
1. Early IUP presumed, 5w4d.
2. Referrals to OB (her prior group) and MFM today, with the genetics letter attached, for early and detailed anatomy scans. Also flagged the 2019 short cervix for cervical length surveillance.
3. GDM risk (BMI 32, grandmother with DM) - OB will decide on early glucose screening.
4. Continue prenatal vitamin.
5. This replaces her physical this year; we'll catch up on preventive care after delivery.
She knows to message any time.

documents.title: Referrals and refill
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: OB intake confirmed for 6/17. MFM office called: they have the genetics letter and will book her detailed anatomy scan around 20 weeks; OB to coordinate the earlier scans. Pt also asked for a prenatal vitamin refill - pended for PCP.

documents.title: Refill sent
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Prenatal vitamin with iron, 90 days x 3 refills, sent.

documents.title: Maternal-fetal medicine ultrasound and consult (visit date 09/08/2025)
documents.author: maternal-fetal medicine
documents.body:
MATERNAL-FETAL MEDICINE - DETAILED FETAL ANATOMY ULTRASOUND
Regional hospital MFM service
Date of service: 09/08/2025
Patient: Robin Parsons, 34 y/o G3P1101 at 20w1d (LMP 4/20/2025, consistent with first-trimester ultrasound)
Indication: Prior pregnancy affected by perinatal lethal osteogenesis imperfecta (heterozygous COL1A1 pathogenic variant, presumed de novo); prior short cervix.

Findings: Single live intrauterine pregnancy, cardiac activity present. Biometry concordant with dates. Detailed survey of fetal anatomy is normal. Long bones (femurs, humeri, tibiae/fibulae, radii/ulnae) are of normal length, contour and echogenicity bilaterally with no fractures, bowing or angulation. Thorax normal in size and shape; ribs normal. Skull normally mineralized. Heart, abdomen, kidneys, spine and face normal. Placenta anterior, no previa. Amniotic fluid normal.
Transvaginal cervical length: 38 mm, no funneling.

Impression: Normal detailed anatomy survey at 20w1d with a normal-appearing fetal skeleton. Normal cervical length.
Plan: Reassurance provided; findings reviewed with Ms. Parsons and her husband. Continue routine prenatal care with her OB group, glucose screening per OB. We are glad to see her again if any concern arises.

Maternal-Fetal Medicine
cc: OB/GYN; PCP

documents.title: MFM report reviewed
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Detailed anatomy at 20w1d normal - long bones normal, no fractures, normal chest. CL 38 mm. Sent Robin a short note.

documents.title: Your MFM scan
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Robin, I just read the MFM report from Monday. What a relief to see in writing - normal bones, normal chest, normal cervix length. Thinking of you.

documents.title: RE: Your MFM scan
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Thank you so much. I cried in the parking lot (good tears). See you for my flu shot.

documents.body: Flu vaccine, pt ~24 wks pregnant. Screening negative, no prior reactions. Influenza trivalent 0.5 mL IM R deltoid, VIS given. Tolerated without issue. Plans updated COVID at pharmacy; OB to give Tdap and RSV later in pregnancy.

documents.title: Obstetrics prenatal visit, 27 weeks (visit date 10/27/2025) with OGTT
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
OUTSIDE OB/GYN GROUP - PRENATAL VISIT
Date of service: 10/27/2025 (addendum 10/31/2025)
Patient: Robin Parsons, 34 y/o G3P1101 at 27w1d

OB history: term SVD 2020 (short cervix noted at 22 weeks that pregnancy); 2022 pregnancy affected by perinatal lethal osteogenesis imperfecta (COL1A1, presumed de novo), delivered at 23w6d, stillbirth. This pregnancy: normal MFM detailed anatomy at 20 weeks, cervical length 38 mm.

Interval: Here for routine prenatal care. Over the past 2 weeks she has noticed being thirstier than usual and urinating more. Denies vaginal bleeding, contractions, or leakage of fluid. Active fetal movement.

Medications: prenatal vitamin with iron 1 tab daily. Allergies: NKDA.
PMH: obesity, pre-pregnancy BMI 32. PSH: none.
Family history: type 2 diabetes (maternal grandmother).
Social: teacher, never smoker, no alcohol.

BP 128/78. FHT normal.

Labs: 1-hour 50 g glucose challenge today: 190 mg/dL. Fasting glucose drawn: 98 mg/dL.

Addendum 10/31/2025: 3-hour 100 g oral glucose tolerance test - fasting 95 mg/dL, 1 hour 180 mg/dL, 2 hours 155 mg/dL, 3 hours 140 mg/dL. All four values meet Carpenter-Coustan criteria. Diagnosis: gestational diabetes mellitus.

Plan: Diagnosis reviewed with patient by phone. Medical nutrition therapy referral with our diabetes educator (seen 11/3); glucose meter, strips and lancets prescribed; check fasting and 1-hour postprandial glucose four times daily and bring logs. Activity after meals encouraged. Follow-up in 1-2 weeks with log review; growth ultrasound later in third trimester.

cc: PCP

documents.title: Outside OB note reviewed
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: GDM: GCT 190, OGTT 95/180/155/140 (10/31). Diet + home glucose monitoring per OB, no meds. Added to problem list. Postpartum OGTT will be needed - will plan with OB.

documents.title: Gestational diabetes question
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi, I'm sure you saw I have gestational diabetes now. Does this mean I'll get type 2 like my grandma? The finger sticks are fine, just annoying with a classroom of kids. Also I got the updated covid shot 10/18 at the pharmacy, forgot to tell you.

documents.title: RE: Gestational diabetes question
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Robin. I did see it. Gestational diabetes usually goes away after delivery. It does raise the chance of type 2 diabetes later in life, so after the baby comes we'll do a glucose tolerance test at about 6-12 weeks and then check an A1c every year or few years. A lot of what you're doing now - the food changes and the walking - is exactly what lowers that risk long-term. Hang in there with the finger sticks. COVID shot recorded.

documents.title: Labor & delivery discharge summary (admitted 01/18/2026)
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
REGIONAL HOSPITAL - OBSTETRIC DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admit: 01/18/2026  Discharge: 01/21/2026
Patient: Robin Parsons, 34 y/o G3P1101 -> G3P2102
Attending: Obstetrics

Admission: 39w0d, presented to labor and delivery in active labor after about 14 hours of contractions at home and in triage. Cervix 4 cm on admission. Amniotomy performed; two hours later little change. She was uncomfortable and asked for pain relief. Exam at that time: 5 cm, 80% effaced, -2 station, occiput posterior. Fetal heart tracing category I. Tocodynamometry showed irregular contractions of varying strength.

Antepartum history: Gestational diabetes, diet-controlled. Pre-pregnancy BMI 32. Prior term vaginal delivery (2020); 2022 pregnancy affected by perinatal lethal osteogenesis imperfecta, delivered at 23w6d. Normal detailed anatomy this pregnancy. GBS negative.

Labor course: Epidural placed with good relief. Intrauterine pressure catheter placed and oxytocin augmentation started. She progressed to 6 cm and then made no further cervical change over 4 hours despite adequate contractions (greater than 200 MVU). Fetal head remained at -2, occiput posterior. Diagnosis: arrest of dilation in the active phase. Options reviewed; she consented to cesarean delivery.

Procedure 01/18/2026: Primary low transverse cesarean section under epidural anesthesia. Liveborn male at 21:40, 3,520 g, Apgars 8 and 9. Newborn glucose checks normal. EBL 800 mL. No complications.

Postpartum course: Uncomplicated. Ambulating, tolerating diet, incision clean and dry. Glucose checks not required after delivery given diet-controlled GDM. Hgb appropriate.

Discharge diagnoses: Arrest of dilation (prolonged labor), primary low transverse cesarean delivery; gestational diabetes, diet-controlled, resolved with delivery; liveborn male.
Discharge medications: ibuprofen 600 mg every 6 hours as needed; acetaminophen 500 mg, 1-2 tablets every 6 hours as needed; prenatal vitamin with iron daily.
Allergies: NKDA.
Follow-up: OB incision check at 2 weeks and postpartum visit at 6 weeks. 75 g 2-hour OGTT at 4-12 weeks postpartum (PCP or OB).
cc: PCP

documents.title: Discharge summary reviewed
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Delivered 1/18 by primary C/S for arrest of dilation at 6 cm after augmentation; healthy boy 3,520 g. GDM resolved - hx GDM added. Postpartum OGTT - we'll order at her visit. RN call tomorrow; PCP visit ~5 wks.

documents.title: Post-discharge call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Called pt 2 days after discharge. Congratulated. Pain controlled with ibuprofen and acetaminophen, using less each day. Incision dry, no redness or drainage. Afebrile. Bleeding moderate and decreasing. No calf pain, headache or vision change; BP at L&D was fine. Feeding going OK. Mood: tired, happy. OB incision check booked 2/2. Scheduled PCP visit 2/24. Reviewed reasons to call: fever, wound redness/drainage, heavy bleeding, leg swelling, severe headache, low mood.

documents.title: Office Visit - Postpartum Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Robin, 35, 5 wks after primary C/S (1/18) for arrest of dilation; son doing well. Diet-controlled GDM this pregnancy.

Recovery: incision healing, OB checked it 2/2 and was happy. Off ibuprofen and acetaminophen for about two weeks. Bleeding now just spotting. No fevers. Thirst and frequent urination have resolved since delivery. Breastfeeding. Sleep in chunks; husband and 6-year-old daughter adjusting. On leave until April.

PHQ-9 3. No SI. Feels very different from 2022, she says.

Meds: prenatal vitamin with iron daily. NKDA.

Exam: Vitals as charted. Well appearing. Heart regular. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, Pfannenstiel incision well healed, no erythema or tenderness. Calves soft, nontender. Affect bright.

A/P
1. Postpartum after cesarean - recovering well.
2. Hx GDM: 75 g 2-hour OGTT at 7 weeks postpartum, ordered for 3/10 (fasting). If normal, A1c every 1-3 years; lifelong higher risk for T2DM discussed.
3. Obesity class I: postpartum weight expected to come down with time; revisit at physical.
4. Mood screen reassuring; reviewed postpartum depression symptoms.
5. Continue prenatal vitamin while breastfeeding.
6. Annual physical this fall.

documents.title: Obstetrics postpartum visit (visit date 03/02/2026)
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
OUTSIDE OB/GYN GROUP - POSTPARTUM VISIT
Date of service: 03/02/2026
Patient: Robin Parsons, 35 y/o G3P2102, 6 weeks after primary low transverse cesarean (01/18/2026) for arrest of dilation.

Doing well. Lochia resolved. Breastfeeding. Pain resolved, off analgesics. Mood good; EPDS low risk.
History of diet-controlled GDM - postpartum OGTT being done through her PCP.

BP normal. Abdomen soft; Pfannenstiel incision well healed. Pelvic exam deferred per patient preference; no concerns.

Assessment: Normal postpartum recovery after cesarean.
Plan: Resume normal activity. Family planning discussed; she will let us know. Routine gynecologic care; Pap/HPV per PCP schedule (last 2023 normal). Interpregnancy interval counseling given prior cesarean.

cc: PCP
